claims.text: The target multiphase metallic alloys initially have coarse grains.
The target alloys initially have unstable phase distributions.
A machine-learning framework can use historical experimental and simulation data to predict optimal thermo-mechanical processing sequences.
Temperature profiles, deformation rates, and aging durations can be jointly optimized by the proposed machine-learning framework.
Appropriate post-process heat treatments provide stress relief after room- or moderate-temperature processing.
Reliable optimization requires a sufficiently comprehensive training dataset covering the relevant processing window.
Machine-learning-guided thermo-mechanical processing will produce ultrafine grains.
Optimized processing will stabilize phase boundaries through tailored precipitation and transformation processes.
The machine-learning model can correlate processing parameters with phase-distribution evolution.
The machine-learning model can correlate processing parameters with grain-size evolution.
The identified process windows will suppress unwanted phase transformations.
The identified process windows will suppress grain coarsening.
Targeted control of microstructure and phase structure can improve mechanical performance.
Machine-learning-guided samples will have greater phase stability than conventionally processed samples.
Machine-learning-guided samples will have finer, ultrafine grains relative to conventionally processed samples.
Machine-learning-guided samples will exhibit increased strength and ductility relative to samples processed by trial and error.
The framework's effectiveness may be limited to alloy systems and processing conditions represented in its training data.
Extrapolation beyond the represented training regime introduces higher predictive uncertainty.
